authored_operations: Replace exact/prefix-only SourceMux with source pattern parsing, duplicate/conflict relationships, host/method precedence, GET-to-HEAD fallback, literal/single/multi/{$} patterns and byte-preserving named captures.

Modern not-found versus sorted 405 Allow (including trailing-slash candidates), request matched-pattern projection, all-method legacy literal/longest-prefix host routing and RequestURI * mux rejection.

Canonicalize escaped modern paths and decoded legacy paths, preserve escaped segment boundaries and query values, strip valid host ports, and keep CONNECT separate URL.Host versus Request.Host matching.

Explicit Go121 compatibility profile uses 301. BOTH Go1.26.5 and Go1.27.1 modern sources use 307. Go126 retains its decoded/escaped redirect construction, while Go127 uses urlFromEscaped to preserve encoded separators and avoid double escaping.
Redirect Location non-ASCII escaping, HTML link escaping, existing Content-Type behavior, GET/HEAD content-type and GET-only short body including the second newline.

Incoming request retains decoded URL bytes and source RawPath/default-escape distinction alongside the old text view. Malformed path escapes return 400 before callbacks. CONNECT authority-form has empty URL.Path.

Native informational response path: source writer -> bounded per-request InformationalSender -> existing H1 driver/encoder/flush acknowledgement or existing H2 stream SendResponse::send_informational. Intermediate headers leave the final response and handler header map uncommitted and uncleared.

HTTP/1 101 remains a final upgrade response; bundled Go HTTP/2 treats its 1xx class separately. HTTP/1 explicit 100 or final headers disable deferred automatic Continue. HTTP/2 body-read Continue remains its separate source state, including source Expect removal and multi-value token rules.

Server-level OPTIONS * bypasses mux dispatch, emits zero Content-Length, drains up to the source 4KB bound and closes an oversized HTTP/1 connection. Unknown HTTP/1 expectations produce the source empty 417 with Connection close before user handlers.

Full ordered 512-byte Go sniff table includes HTML/XML/PDF/PostScript/BOM/images/audio/video/MP4/fonts/archives/WASM/text. Detection uses the first emitted buffered chunk, not the first small handler write.

ResponseWriter now owns source 2048-byte H1 and 4096-byte H2 buffering, direct large writes, header snapshots and no-body/HEAD/header-presence/Content-Encoding/Transfer-Encoding decisions. H1 signed length parsing and H2 deferred unsigned-63-bit parsing retain their distinct count/error and empty-write behavior.

Attempted int64 write count wraps and includes rejected length overruns; failed transport writes retain the original error chain through one shared sticky failure. Header transport failures are ignored as in source WriteHeader, while the native connection retains its failure.

Source clock and default HTTP diagnostic capabilities are statically supplied by UtilityRuntimeProviders. Date is generated only when its header key is absent, with native automatic dates disabled; Go status-line strings and unknown-code fallback are supplied to the existing reason-phrase extension.

Hyper H2 stream/upgrade futures now use a weak executor and the existing per-connection UtilityTaskScope. Normal/error connection exits cancel and join protocol children; emergency scope Drop aborts owned children. No discarded TokioExecutor JoinHandles or competing lifecycle manager.

Trailer declarations now follow source comma/ASCII-space splitting, canonicalization and the exact httpguts forbidden-name table. H1 retains duplicate declarations and prefixed fields; H2 de-duplicates and promotes prefixed fields with unordered canonical-key collision choices.

Actual response trailer I/O: ResponseWriter publishes one source-encoded H1 field block before yielding its trailers frame. The pinned native connection consumes it only for this response's chunked body, independent of client TE or prior Trailer declarations. Source Header.Write sorting, key spelling, CR/LF replacement and trimming are authored. H2 emits actual trailers frames through the existing h2 body sender, including key-presence with empty values.

Bounded response messages now carry end-of-stream decisions. HTTP/2 HEAD and completed empty responses can end on HEADERS, final data can carry END_STREAM, and present trailers end on their HEADERS frame. This is authored source control flow, not a native frame/parity observation.

Source HTTP/2 Connection first-value exactly close removes that field and signals its connection-owned graceful-close token. The existing Hyper connection driver owns shutdown/GOAWAY and independent stream draining; no new server or task manager.

Plain and TLS accept loops share one per-listener AcceptBackoff, 5ms doubling to 1s, reset on success, via static CGP SourceHttpDelay. Error handling checks shutdown before retry and retains permanent native errors. The source syscall-wrapped Unix/Windows Errno policy is distinct from the direct-Errno exception and Winsock lookalikes; native error-origin and display profiles remain open.

Original transport RequestBody remains one owner for Incoming, pending data, trailers, remaining/closed/EOF/early-close state and H2 close/read wakeup. Current Request.Body and expectation-wrapper flags are now distinct retained owners described below.

HTTP/1 pre-response discard now retains the 256KB threshold and separate limit+1 read rule. H1 Close uses its distinct strict-greater-than size rule, fixed copy bound, early-close flag and request-closing/chunked branch. OPTIONS reads at most its remaining 4KB limit plus one source byte per call. Body Close is async and the existing FourZeroFour caller awaits it after the successful-read/error-response path.

Source H1 framing decisions now include inferred lengths, HEAD/no-body suppression, identity versus chunked transfer, conflicting Transfer-Encoding/Content-Length handling, HTTP/1.0 keep-alive and close rules, Continue-reader EOF, source full-duplex opt-in, Date/sniff/header-key presence and protocol-switch Connection preservation. The source handler fields and extraHeader fields remain separate output stages; the latter use Date/length/type/connection/transfer order.

SourceResponse carries immutable H1 fields/framing into the existing native role/connection encoder. Normal and informational source fields use Go Header.Write byte normalization, original key spelling and sorted map order. Source chunks use lowercase hex. Source Content-Length mode does not add native truncation, a competing attempted-byte counter, or an early body-end decision; the source writer retains wrapping/rejected-write accounting.

SourceResponseEnd is published once by the existing request phase after handler return and body cleanup, with declared-length/attempted-count, write-failure, close-after-reply and early-body-close decisions. The existing H1 driver waits before reuse, including HEAD/no-body replies, and preserves queued I/O. Emergency request-phase Drop publishes close. No new actor, executor, registry or lifecycle manager.

Connection disposal now cancels its request children through the existing connection phase. Normal H1 response-body disposal no longer cancels a still-running no-body handler; H2 keeps independent stream/body disposal cancellation. Production parent/source-profile and native schedule reconciliation remain open.

Source H1 heads now bypass the native response-metadata keep-alive heuristic, including separately encoded HTTP/1.0 extra fields. Explicit native shutdown is retained and cannot be re-enabled by a source head. Source close-delimited output likewise defers physical close to handler/body-cleanup completion rather than ending that phase at byte EOF.

Headers now retains raw byte names, nil-map identity and shared map descriptors; HeaderValues retains nil versus non-nil empty, an independent length/capacity/offset view and one shared backing owner. Map clone, shallow copy and source deep copy are distinct operations. Indexed writes and in-capacity append retain aliases; growth allocates separate backing. Value iteration reads shared slots rather than an eager value snapshot.

H1 response snapshots use Header.Clone's combined backing and clipped per-key capacities, nil-value preservation and source-int total-count behavior. Bundled H2 uses its separate per-key clone and nil-to-non-nil-empty rule. Informational filtering uses a new map without clearing the handler map. Native H1 header serialization still sorts raw keys independently of source map iteration.

Header append capacity has explicit Go1.26 word32/word64 and heap-address parameters, signed nextslicecap arithmetic, pointer-containing string size-class/header rounding and source-word page-rounding overflow. The current constructor explicitly selects Go126/64/48; actual source tool/ABI/configuration binding remains M0027, without Rust-host capacity inference.

Source LogRequest now retains the redacted header map as SourceLogValue::HttpHeaders until the existing CGP logger serializes. Non-sensitive value arrays remain shared, sensitive values are independent REDACTED slices, and WithField replaces the typed field normally. Header JSON retains nil/null versus empty arrays/maps, raw-byte key sort, duplicate keys after UTF8 replacement, per-invalid-byte escaped UFFFD versus literal valid UFFFD, HTML and JS-separator escaping through the already enabled serde_json RawValue capability.

Requests initialize declared trailer maps with nil values and source H1/H2 forbidden/empty-element rules, retain non-chunked H1 Trailer headers, remove selected trailer declarations from the request header map and merge actual trailers into the same map owner. H2 request Cookie lines join with semicolon-space. Request, response, trailer, gateway and logging consumers use the same typed header data.

HttpRequest and ResponseWriter share RequestFields for live method bytes, ContentLength and current Body. Mux, gateway method override, APIServer GET dispatch and HTTP response framing read that shared owner; pre-handler wantsClose/wants10 snapshots remain intentional.

SourceBody retains NoBody, native, H1 expectContinueReader, H2 reader, io.NopCloser(bytes.Reader), nil or one custom SourceReadCloser receiver. Cloning retains the interface receiver/cursor; replacing Request.Body does not mutate the retained original body or close the replacement during server cleanup.

H1 framing inspects current Body type/closed/remaining/expect-EOF state, but io.CopyN discard and finishRequest Close use the original response.reqBody. The final early-close type assertion applies only to the current native H1 Body, excluding expectation wrappers and custom readers.

SourceBodyRead retains data and an optional exact EOF/failure category together. Native known-length H1 reads pair their last data with EOF while holding the body lock; expectation EOF is set from that read result. H2 keeps its subsequent-read EOF behavior. Empty successful reads are not EOF.

H1 automatic Continue Read and final/explicit-100 disable share the same lock; its available flag clears after flush. Replacing Body bypasses the old wrapper; a retained old wrapper still owns its closed/EOF state. H2 clears needsContinue before sending and before checking its pipe.

ReadAll retains its initial Reader, starts at 512 logical source bytes, applies source byte-slice nextslicecap/noscan size-class growth and consumes returned bytes before an error. Its low-level result retains partial bytes on failure. Form parsing wraps the retained Reader with a 10MiB+1 limit, preserving ReadAll error precedence before size rejection.

SourceJsonDecoder is shared by webhook and gateway consumers: retain the Reader, compact only on refill, grow logical capacity by 2*cap+512, scan data before its paired read error, and discard that local error if a value completes. Sticky framing/read failures and successful semantic decoding remain separate.

H1 byte suppression and final length/reuse checks read the current Method; a previously selected chunked response still emits its final chunk after Method becomes HEAD. Source Empty headers use a native unframed body kept alive through the source phase, allowing subsequent Method reassignment without native length-zero truncation.

SourceByteString and SourceLogValue::Bytes preserve original method/body bytes until Go JSON escaping, including per-invalid-byte escapes. FourZeroFour captures the successful-path deferred Body receiver before logging/writing; the existing CGP body-I/O capability closes that retained receiver.
